dimensions.note: The basic-auth hash, the TLS key and certificate, and inline upload content are sensitive-marked inputs wired from the vault; they reach the host over stdin and land in root-only files (key 0600 root, htpasswd 0640 root:www-data). A private key goes into a short-lived ssh-agent over stdin and a password through an askpass helper, never argv. No content hash is put on any local argv or remote script text (compared locally). Live: 0 hits for the password, its hash or a TLS key line across three rounds of ps argv samples, the scratch repo's .swamp/ and its inputs. Literal-secret echo under --json is the platform limitation (ruling 3); README examples use vault references only. Strict host-key pins are required; insecure_tofu is not offered. Transport is the canonical vendored ssh.ts (fe0139f0).
One info line per install after the host is known good; errors name the failing step (nginx -t stderr excerpt, rollback failures listed by label). No secret or content is logged.

install snapshots the site, enabled link, default site, TLS files and htpasswd before any change; any failure after the snapshot (nginx -t, a credential write, enable/start, an unexpected wildcard listener) restores every one, removes a root the run created, re-runs nginx -t and reports each rollback failure; restore checks every rm/ln exit code and a failed snapshot read refuses before mutation. Persistence happens only after the host is good. Live: a failed credential write rolled /etc/nginx back byte-identical with no reload, and removed the created root (3cbf14d R5).

Unit, regression and model tests over an in-memory fake remote that drives the real shell scripts' semantics: layout grammar, nginx rendering, TLS validation, observation parsing, newline and symlink smuggling, rollback paths, upload caps, default-site restore, wildcard-listener detection and the plain-object method context. Live on a throwaway Ubuntu 24.04 VPS: d8a643a 12/12 (found two Highs), 3cbf14d 5/6 (nginx left disabled), 7b9e4f1 5/5 including a real reboot (enabled, private address only, no wildcard listener in 860 samples).

Re-install with the same inputs changes no file (same MainPID, live); a repeated pinned fetch returns changed: false; a second unref and a second uninstall are no-ops (live: identical stat listing, MainPID and reload count). The reload always runs on install so a retry after a failed reload picks up the config.

The on-disk layout is the contract: sha256/<hex>/<name>, bundles/<tree-hash>/, refs/, SHA256SUMS and .layout-version; URLs derive from the recorded url_base. The tree hash is SHA-256 over sorted '<sha>  <name>' lines in C locale, and verify recomputes it on the host byte for byte (live: matched an independent local computation). Observed tool output (ss, systemctl, stat) is projected, never strictly parsed.

uninstall removes the site, enabled link, TLS files and htpasswd, restores the package default site install removed (only when absent), and removes the served root only with remove_data and only when it is a real directory holding the sentinel; it never removes the nginx package. Residuals (LOGBOOK): purging nginx leaves the enable link install created; the stored removed_default_site flag can restore a default site the operator removed after a first uninstall.

Manifest @randybias/artifact-server 2026.10.17.1, one model, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt. Fixtures use documentation addresses and .test names; the LOGBOOK redacts every real address and hostname. Leak scan, gitleaks (including the branch history) and fixture guard pass. The model is a plain export const model = { ... } literal so the registry catalogs it (merge prep).

Strict argument schemas: root needs two or more segments, no ./.. and no bare system directory (live: /etc refused at validation); file names, refs and hashes have grammars; the realm is restricted; fetch is https-only without userinfo or shell metacharacters. Inline content is capped at 128 MiB (base64 4*ceil(N/3)), because swamp holds payloads in memory before the method runs (live: 200 MiB crashed swamp); larger files use the host-side pinned fetch.
config, server, artifact, listing and verification are infinite with garbage collection 5-10 versions; prune_plan lives 1d.
render_config, install, get, sync, uninstall; upload, fetch, publish_bundle, ref, unref, list; verify, plan_prune, prune. All live-exercised.

Every destructive method enforces its own preconditions against its actual arguments (ruling on workflow resume): install refuses a populated root without a regular sentinel, prune refuses when the recomputed plan hash differs from the approved one and refuses symlinked sha256/<hex> or bundles/<hex> entries, fetch refuses a pin mismatch and removes its temp. Residual (LOGBOOK): bundles/ itself as a symlink yields an empty plan rather than a refusal; nothing outside the root is touched (live).
One generic definition; stored data is keyed by the canonical target plus root, never the definition name, and keys contain no '/', '..' or NUL.

Reads only its own config resource (url_base, default-site snapshot) via context.readResource, proven in the live runtime (uninstall restored the default site from it). Every read-only method persists its observation as a resource.
First release; layout version 1 is recorded in .layout-version so a later layout change can detect and migrate.
